#2157. Calciomercato no stop - Indiscrezioni, trattative e retroscena del 10 novembre

INTER, CALHANOGLU PUÒ RINNOVARE. LAVORI IN CORSO PER IL NUOVO ACCORDO CON THURAM. CISSE RIMANE AL MILAN, RIFIUTATE DUE PROPOSTE. COMO, IDEA MALO GUSTO CON I BUONI RAPPORTI INSIEME AL CHELSEA. JUVENTUS, NON BASTANO GLI ATTACCANTI CHE HA SPALLETTI: PENSIERO FISSO CON SORLOTH. TUTTI GLI OBIETTIVI DEL NAPOLI PER RIPARTIRE A GENNAIO, ALLEGRI HA UNA PRIORITÀ. ROMA, ENDRICK CHIODO FISSO E SPUNTA BALDE COME IDEA DEL MERCATO INVERNALE.

Il tema del rinnovo di contratto di Hakan Calhanoglu è tornato improvvisamente d'attualità in casa Inter, la volontà comune è quella di proseguire insieme e tentare di chiudere l'accordo al più presto, persino entro Natale se si incastreranno tutti i tasselli. Si tratta di un segnale distensivo fondamentale dopo un periodo turbolento iniziato ad agosto: durante la tournée australiana, infatti, il centrocampista turco aveva manifestato qualche perplessità sulla mancanza di contatti per il prolungamento e il timore di non essere più considerato centrale nelle strategie del club, pur ribadendo il forte legame con Milano, l'Inter e i tifosi e forte della fiducia incondizionata del tecnico Cristian Chivu. Ritrovata la serenità ed eseguito il primo passo con la riapertura del dialogo, il vero nodo resta tuttavia di natura economica. Attualmente legato ai nerazzurri fino al 2027 a circa 6,5 milioni netti a stagione, Calhanoglu punta a un nuovo biennale con un ingaggio da top player; dal canto suo, la società mira a ridurre la quota fissa degli stipendi tenendo conto dell'età e dei recenti guai fisici del classe '94. La trattativa rimane dunque aperta e richiederà la giusta intesa tra le parti per arrivare alla fumata bianca.

In casa Inter si lavora per blindare Marcus Thuram: il club nerazzurro ha infatti avviato i primi contatti per prolungare l'accordo con l'attaccante francese, attualmente in scadenza nel 2028, con l'obiettivo di estenderlo fino al 2031. La trattativa si preannuncia tuttavia in salita per motivi economici: la società guidata in panchina da Cristian Chivu vorrebbe proporre una ristrutturazione dell'ingaggio basata su una quota fissa da 4,5-5 milioni di euro integrata da premi e benefit, a fronte dello stipendio attuale da 6,5 milioni che con i bonus sfiora gli 8 milioni a stagione. Una formula che per ora non convince la punta, decisa a non ridimensionare le proprie condizioni contrattuali pur ribadendo la priorità assoluta di vestire la maglia dell'Inter, pur in presenza dei fari puntati da diversi club esteri per l'estate. La forte spinta dei dirigenti verso il rinnovo è legata a doppio filo al rendimento sul campo: dall'infortunio di Lautaro Martinez, Thuram si è preso il peso dell'attacco collezionando quattro gol e due assist in sei gare di campionato, confermandosi elemento imprescindibile nello scacchiere tattico nerazzurro.

Alphadjo Cisse non ha nascosto l'entusiasmo per il suo travolgente inizio di stagione con la maglia del Milan: l'attaccante rossonero ha confidato come la tripletta messa a segno in Europa League sia stata la conferma di poter stare a questi livelli, vivendola non come un punto d'arrivo ma come una promessa mantenuta al bambino che era, consapevole dei propri mezzi e molto esigente con se stesso nonostante il recente lungo infortunio e la giovane età. Una fiducia ricambiata appieno dalla società di via Aldo Rossi che, a pochi mesi dall'arrivo del giocatore, è già al lavoro con i suoi agenti per blindarlo e respingere le sirene di mercato, in particolare quelle del Brighton che sta bussando alla porta con offerte milionarie: l'obiettivo del Milan è infatti quello di adeguare le condizioni contrattuali di Cisse, portando l'ingaggio attuale da circa 800 mila euro al doppio e prolungando la scadenza oltre l'attuale termine del 30 giugno 2030.

Il Como potrebbe inserirsi nella corsa per Malo Gusto: il club lariano, rivelazione della Champions League, avrebbe messo nel mirino il terzino destro classe 2003 del Chelsea, il quale sarebbe pronto a valutare un cambio di scenario nella prossima finestra di mercato pur di trovare più spazio in prima squadra e difendere il proprio ruolo centrale in ottica nazionale francese. Dal canto loro, i Blues non avrebbero chiuso la porta a un addio già a gennaio, complice una discontinuità testimoniata dalle zero presenze da titolare nelle ultime sei uscite di Premier League per l'ex Lione, arrivato a Londra nel 2023. Per accaparrarsi il talento transalpino, apprezzato per giovane età, spinta sulla fascia e ampi margini di crescita, il Como dovrà tuttavia superare la agguerrita concorrenza internazionale di Atletico Madrid, Milan e Lipsia, pronte a scatenare un'asta qualora i dirigenti inglesi aprano definitivamente alla cessione a titolo definitivo o in prestito.

La Juventus continua a valutare opzioni per il mercato di riparazione di gennaio ed è pronta a tornare alla carica per Alexander Sorloth: nonostante i lievi segnali di crescita mostrati da Nick Woltemade e Randal Kolo Muani, i bianconeri intendono regalare al tecnico Luciano Spalletti una punta forte fisicamente e abile ad attaccare la profondità, riallacciando i contatti per il centravanti norvegese dell'Atletico Madrid già concretamente seguito a giugno con un viaggio in Norvegia del direttore sportivo Marco Ottolini. Pur apprezzato da Diego Simeone dopo aver superato i guai fisici di inizio stagione, l'attaccante ex Lipsia non è considerato intoccabile dai Colchoneros e vorrebbe maggior spazio; forte degli ottimi rapporti tra i club - e con la posizione di Jonathan David, attualmente a Madrid in prestito dalla Juve, che potrebbe incidere nelle dinamiche -, la società torinese mantiene attiva la pista, pur monitorando profili alternativi come Gianluca Scamacca, Mateo Retegui e Folarin Balogun, quest'ultimo già proposto in estate da Jorge Mendes.

Il Napoli ha già iniziato a pianificare le strategie per la sessione invernale di calciomercato: la dirigenza azzurra è al lavoro per mettere a disposizione del tecnico Massimiliano Allegri quattro rinforzi mirati - nello specifico un centravanti, un esterno d'attacco e due centrocampisti -, un piano che potrebbe essere accompagnato anche da alcune uscite per ridisegnare l'organico in vista della seconda parte di stagione. Per l'attacco il profilo in cima alle preferenze è quello del ventunenne Gustavo Varela, protagonista di un avvio di campionato straordinario con la maglia del Monza che lo vede guidare la classifica marcatori di Serie A con nove reti (undici totali in stagione) ed essere premiato con la chiamata della nazionale portoghese, mentre sull'esterno resta vivo l'interesse per il ventiduenne Jamie Bynoe-Gittens, in uscita dal Chelsea e gradito anche per questioni di lista. Infine, per il reparto mediano i fari sono puntati sul giovane talento del Sassuolo Darryl Bakola, che compirà 19 anni a fine novembre, ma il vero sogno e priorità assoluta rimane Mamadou Coulibaly, classe 2004 del Monaco, per il quale tuttavia la valutazione di circa 40 milioni di euro pretesa dai francesi rende la trattativa assai complessa pur senza scoraggiare i dirigenti partenopei.

Il futuro di Endrick al Real Madrid si trova a un bivio in vista della sessione invernale di calciomercato: il ventenne, attaccante brasiliano, sta valutando seriamente di lasciare i blancos a gennaio per ritrovare continuità ed evitare di rallentare la propria crescita. Nonostante l'ottimo rapporto con José Mourinho, che in estate ne aveva bloccato il trasferimento alla Roma, la punta ha collezionato soltanto 140 minuti spalmati su 7 presenze, ripercorrendo l'inizio della scorsa stagione prima che il prestito al Lione gli permettesse di esplodere con 8 gol e 7 assist in 21 gare e conquistare la chiamata al Mondiale con la Seleçao del CT Carlo Ancelotti. Sulle sue tracce resta vigile la Roma, ma la concorrenza più agguerrita è quella dello Sporting guidato proprio da Paulo Fonseca, il tecnico che lo aveva valorizzato in Francia e che saprebbe offrirgli garanzie d'impiego, la vetrina della Champions League e un ambientamento facilitato dalla lingua; dal canto suo, la dirigenza del Real Madrid non intende ostacolare la partenza per tutelare un investimento superiore agli 80 milioni ed evitare svalutazioni, mentre dal ritiro del Brasile lo stesso Endrick ha ribadito con maturo affetto la propria priorità, dichiarando di apprezzare la vicinanza umana di Mourinho ma di voler solo giocare e dare un reale impulso alla propria carriera.

In casa Roma l'avvio di campionato ha certificato ambizioni da scudetto: dopo undici giornate la squadra ha dimostrato di avere i numeri per lottare fino in fondo e la finestra invernale di calciomercato rappresenta l'occasione perfetta per puntellare la rosa a disposizione di Gian Piero Gasperini con un paio di innesti di spessore. Tra i profili finiti nel mirino del direttore sportivo Tony D’Amico c'è Alejandro Balde, esterno sinistro classe 2003 in forza al Barcellona; il club catalano potrebbe aprire alla cessione già a gennaio per fare cassa e investire su un difensore centrale, vera priorità del tecnico Hansi Flick. Incassato il pieno gradimento di Gasperini, lo scoglio principale per i giallorossi rimane la formula dell'operazione - con l'ipotesi di un prestito oneroso con obbligo di riscatto condizionato alla qualificazione in Champions League -, resa complessa da un'alta valutazione del cartellino e da un ingaggio di rilievo. A complicare ulteriormente i piani della Roma c'è poi l'affollata concorrenza internazionale scatenata dall'apertura dei blaugrana: in Premier League si muovono Liverpool, Aston Villa, Manchester United, Manchester City e Tottenham, in Ligue 1 c'è il Monaco, mentre in Italia anche la Juventus valuta l'opzione nell'eventualità di un addio di Andrea Cambiaso, rendendo il terzino spagnolo uno dei pezzi pregiati più contesi della imminente sessione di mercato.

ANTONIO CONTE SORPRENDE: PROCURA A ZAHAVI, VUOLE LO UNITED. LINDELOF RINNOVA CON L'ASTON VILLA, MANCA SOLO L'UFFICIALITÀ PER L'ESONERO DI CAHUZAC DAL LENS, VAN DIJK NON PENSA AL FUTURO PER ORA.

La panchina di Michael Carrick al Manchester United appare ormai sul punto di crollare: secondo le ultime indiscrezioni, l'esonero del tecnico inglese è considerato una semplice questione di tempo nei prossimi giorni, dato che il rocambolesco 4-4 strappato in extremis a Old Trafford contro l'Aston Villa non è bastato a raddrizzare la rotta né a sanare il feeling incrinato con lo spogliatoio. Mentre le quotazioni di Mauricio Pochettino continuavano a salire - con l'attuale commissario tecnico degli Stati Uniti che avrebbe già dato la propria disponibilità a raccogliere il testimone, forte di una clausola rescissoria da 9 milioni di euro per liberarsi dal contratto fino al 2030 con la selezione americana e di una residenza familiare a Londra -, il quadro si è improvvisamente complicato con l'inserimento a sorpresa di Antonio Conte. Il 57enne, allenatore leccese, libero dopo l'addio al Napoli a fine scorsa stagione, si sarebbe infatti affidato al potente agente Pini Zahavi con l'obiettivo specifico di farsi avanti per la guida dei Red Devils; in attesa di capire se la dirigenza di Old Trafford affonderà il colpo prima del doppio impegno di Pochettino nei quarti di Concacaf Nations League contro Haiti, la corsa alla successione di Carrick resta più intricata che mai.

L'Aston Villa blinda Victor Lindelof. Il club inglese ha annunciato di aver esercitato l'opzione presente nel contratto del difensore svedese, prolungando l'accordo fino al 2028. Arrivato a Villa Park nel 2025, l'ex Manchester United ha avuto un impatto immediato, diventando uno dei punti di riferimento della squadra. Nel suo primo anno con la maglia dei Villans è stato protagonista anche nella conquista dell'Europa League, giocando un ruolo importante nella finale vinta 3-0 contro il Friburgo a Istanbul. Lindelöf ha finora disputato 43 partite con la maglia dell'Aston Villa e si è rapidamente affermato al centro della difesa grazie alla sua esperienza e alla capacità di guidare il reparto arretrato. Il classe 1994 continua inoltre a essere anche un elemento fondamentale della nazionale svedese, di cui è il capitano. Con il rinnovo fino al 2028, il club di Birmingham conferma la volontà di puntare ancora sulle sue qualità.

Il Lens si appresta a cambiare nuovamente guida tecnica: nelle prossime ore la società francese ufficializzerà l'esonero di Yannick Cahuzac, maturato dopo la riunione dirigenziale di lunedì sera e motivato da un avvio di stagione condellato da risultati deludenti e devastanti sul piano psicologico. Figura emblematica del club, Cahuzac lascerà definitivamente i Sang et Or senza essere ricollocato in altri ruoli societari dopo un'avventura durata appena due mesi: subentrato il 21 settembre a Dino Toppmoller in seguito al ko con il Monaco (1-2), il tecnico ha visto segnato il proprio destino dal recente k.o. interno contro il Marsiglia (1-2), arrivato a pochi giorni dal pesantissimo 1-9 incassato in Champions League contro il Como, sconfitta che rappresenta la peggiore di sempre per una squadra transalpina nelle coppe europee. Per la successione la dirigenza sta valutando tre profili e tra questi spunta la clamorosa candidatura di Pierre Sage: andato via in estate, l'ex allenatore si trova attualmente in bilico sulla panchina del Crystal Palace, con un esonero imminente in Premier League che potrebbe trasformarlo nella soluzione immediata per restituire stabilità all'ambiente.

Virgil van Dijk non teme di finire in scadenza con il Liverpool al termine della stagione, nonostante i suoi 35 anni. "Se si prolunga, tanto meglio. Altrimenti, andrò altrove. Non c'è nulla da segnalare per il momento, ma questo non significa che sono in panico. Mentalmente sto bene; fisicamente ho avuto un piccolo problema in queste ultime due settimane, ma sto facendo tutto il possibile per essere presente sul campo". Qualsiasi possibilità per il difensore olandese, che a parametro zero farebbe certamente gola a chiunque.

#2155. ‘Definitely’: EFL expert has say on Birmingham City’s top two chances

Birmingham City are sat top of the Championship table after their first 15 fixtures of the season. BCFC are above Middlesbrough and Stoke City on goal difference, with the likes of Wolves, West Brom and Swansea City also chasing them down.

The Blues are back in action after the international break with an away trip to the Bet365 Stadium to take on Stoke City as they aim to keep their momentum going. They beat Swansea City 2-1 at home last time out after a brace by Jay Stansfield.

Elek reckons the Midlands outfit can keep it up and has said on the Not The Top 20 Podcast on YouTube: “They can definitely stay there. There is no reason why they can’t. We’re not talking about a Championship minnow here. We’re talking about a club who have invested a lot of money in their playing squad. They were the best League One squad vs the level we’ve seen in a long time.”

He added: “The ascent Ipswich and Sunderland have shown, and to an extent Coventry although that took a few more seasons, the pathway is already there.”

Birmingham City came up from League One back in 2025 after they stormed to the title. BCFC then spent the last campaign adapting to life in the Championship and fell short of the play-offs.

The Blues stuck with head coach Chris Davies in the summer though and that decision has worked out well for them. They are rock solid at the back and they have the best defensive record in the division at the moment ahead of West Brom and Southampton.

Christoph Klarer and Phil Neumann have both been excellent at the heart of defence, with Alex Cochrane to the left of them. Dael Fry, who joined in the summer after the end of his contract at Middlesbrough, then provides useful back-up from the bench.

Further up the pitch, Jhon Solis, Paik Seung-ho and Tomoki Iwata inject quality into their midfield department. Stansfield, Liam Millar, Patrick Roberts, Demarai Gray and August Priske are all dangerous attackers and can cause serious issues to opposition defenders.

Birmingham City could do with another striker in the January transfer window. BCFC need some competition for Priske with Luis Vazquez struggling to get to grips with English football.

The Blues would also benefit from another attacking midfielder or winger ahead of the second-half of the season. Their pursuit of Joe Gelhardt in the summer was well documented and someone like him would be ideal, although he won’t leave Hull City.

You could also argue that Davies should bring in another central defender this winter too. If Klarer, Neumann or Fry were to get injured, they would be left pretty short of depth in that area.

Birmingham City are on a roll and will be full of confidence. Coventry City and Hull City showed last season that you don’t need parachute payments to go up.

The Blues need to stay grounded though and can’t get too carried away. Their away defeat at Cardiff City last month proved every single match is tough.

#2154. Emergenza Inter, tutti i perché: non c'è un nuovo Pio Esposito ed è costruita per un solo modulo (poco europeo). L'Under 23 ancora non produce e il mercato sta prendendo una direzione diversa

Piove sul bagnato per l'Inter che dopo Ange-Yoan Bonny per circa un mese, perde pure Marcus Thuram. I due si sono fermati dopo l'ultima partita contro il Como e hanno dovuto lasciare i rispettivi ritiri di Costa d'Avorio e Francia. Non solo: Lautaro Martinez tornerà a lavorare pienamente col gruppo solo pochi giorni prima del prossimo impegno contro l'Atalanta e Christian Chivu fa ogni tipo di scongiuro affinché Francesco Pio Esposito torni integro ad Appiano Gentile dopo il doppio (e intenso) impegno con la Nazionale. Le ultime su Thuram dicono che potrebbe essere solo un affaticamento, ma ciò non toglie che la coperta resti corta...

Quattro uomini e due maglie, per un attacco a due punte, è una coperta non corta, non lunga. 'Giusta', verrebbe da dire, ma solo se alle spalle dei giocatori che hai in rosa, in un calcio dal calendario frenetico e così intenso, hai dei giovani pronti. Mattia Mosconi è un esterno di grandissimo talento, un sottopunta che si sta facendo le ossa (è un 2007) tra Primavera e soprattutto Serie C con l'Under 23. Un progetto all'inizio, quello nerazzurro, che per adesso non ha ponti e collegamenti con la prima squadra. Matteo Lavelli è più puntero, più 'Pio' che dieci/undici. In C ha fatto un gol, coi grandi di Chivu s'è visto a sprazzi. E questo è il primo problema (lui è un 2006): da quando l'Inter ha strutturato la seconda squadra, ancora non ci sono calciatori che come ai tempi della Juventus Next Gen siano stati cresciuti e formati per essere subito pronti per i grandi. Sarà questa l'occasione, tra necessità e virtù? Certo è che non c'è un Pio Esposito, visto che mancano i giocatori (come anche Alphadjo Cissè al Milan) che abbiano fatto esperienza in Serie B.

Altro problema. L'Inter è una rosa costruita per vincere in Italia, che ha grandi campioni, che ha un'identità straordinaria. Però negli ultimi tre anni in particolare, il pallone sta prendendo una direzione diversa. E i nerazzurri sono una delle squadre che meno di tutte in Europa saltano l'uomo, che cercano meno il dribbling. Ha una rosa costruita con una sola identità, il 3-5-2, il binario d'Inzaghiana memoria e prima ancora di Contiana tradizione. E su quello (ottimamente) marcia, spedita. Solo che non sta trovando un'alternativa di strategia tattica. Il tentativo maldestro di Chivu nel Derby col Milan lo racconta. In Europa si gioca a quattro dietro e con uomini capaci di creare la superiorità davanti. L'Inter è meravigliosamente preparata ma è abbastanza? Questo, in situazioni d'emergenza, soprattutto in difesa e in attacco, crea dei problemi. Perché non è duttile, perché è rigida, perché è dogmatica e non fluida come il calcio d'oggi imporrebbe. E invece no. E invece nella sfortuna deve più pregare che trovare soluzioni alternative, o cercare giovani che però sta aspettando piuttosto che costruendo con rapidità.

#2153. Candreva e la Lazio: «non ho mai rifiutato» il ruolo di vicecapitano

Pioli gli propose l’incarico in camera; l’ex giocatore ricorda anche l’accoglienza dei tifosi dopo il gol al San Paolo.

Antonio Candreva non ha mai rifiutato di diventare vicecapitano della Lazio. L’ex biancoceleste lo ha chiarito a Crazy Calcio Show, ripercorrendo anche il rapporto con i tifosi e la notte trascorsa senza dormire prima della finale di Coppa Italia contro la Roma. Oggi fa parte dello staff tecnico della Nazionale Under 15.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Candreva ricorda i quattro anni e mezzo alla Lazio come un’esperienza indimenticabile. L’inizio, però, non fu semplice: pesava su di lui una presunta fede romanista. Il gol segnato al San Paolo contro il Napoli segnò una svolta nel rapporto con i sostenitori biancocelesti.

«Quello è stato il momento in cui sono stato accolto dalla Lazio», ha raccontato. Candreva descrive quell’avvicinamento come qualcosa voluto sia da lui sia dal pubblico, una liberazione. Ha aggiunto che la curva biancoceleste era quella capace di dargli più carica in campo e che ancora oggi è felice di aver ricevuto un coro dai tifosi.

L’ex giocatore ha poi smentito la ricostruzione secondo cui avrebbe rinunciato a fare il vicecapitano quando la fascia passò sul braccio di Biglia. «È una storia falsa, perché non pretendevo nulla», ha precisato. Davanti a lui, ha ricordato, c’erano giocatori come Radu, Marchetti e Klose: per questo non si aspettava alcun incarico.

Quando Pioli lo chiamò in camera per proporgli il ruolo, la questione fu discussa insieme. Candreva ha ribadito il punto con parole nette: «non ho mai rifiutato».

#2152. QPR’s Top 3 players of the 2026/27 season so far, including resurgent 6-goal/assist star

QPR sit 8th in the Championship table with the latest international break upon us. The Hoops have had some patchy form in recent weeks, but they enter the break off the back of a 2-1 win over Lincoln City.

Julien Stephan and co will be pleased with their efforts to date, but there’s room for improvement. The time without league football offers the R’s a chance to put some work in on the training ground, while we can assess the season so far and pick out some standout stars.

In no particular order, we put forward QPR’s top three players of the 2026/27 season so far…

Ronnie Edwards’ fine loan at QPR in the 2024/25 season meant they knew what to expect when he returned permanently earlier this year. He reclaimed a key role swiftly, and the 23-year-old has gone from strength to strength this term.

Used in defensive midfield and centre-back by Stephan, Edwards is one of the Hoops’ most influential players. As per FotMob‘s data, he stands out in possession as he ranks among the Championship’s best centre-backs for successful passes (767), long ball completion rate (62.1%), interceptions (20) and recoveries (65).

His best displays include the big home wins over Swansea City and Derby County, and the 0-0 draw at Charlton Athletic. Edwards has been consistent all season though, proving his star quality at this level.

Throughout his second stint at QPR, Paul Smyth has endured some tough spells. After three years, some may have expected the Northern Irishman to be phased out of the first XI by the likes of Harvey Vale, Karamoko Dembele, Kwame Poku or Koki Saito, but that has not been the case.

Smyth has retained a regular role in Stephan’s side, and it is not hard to see why. The resurgent 29-year-old shows the commitment and endeavour Stephan desires from his attackers, and he’s added more end product to his game with three goals and three assists in his 14 league appearances this season.

He is tied with Richard Kone at the top of the goal contribution charts at Loftus Road and ranks in the top three of Hoops players for big chances created (3), xG on target (2.0) and expected assists (1.6). Smyth has also won three penalties – more than any other player in the Championship (FotMob).

Last but not least is Pierce Charles, whose influence from goalkeeper cannot be overrstated. The Northern Irish prospect arrived as a highly-regarded talent on loan from Manchester City after his Sheffield Wednesday breakthrough, and he has not disappointed.

Charles has work to do with his shot-stopping, as shown by an xG prevented of -2.47 and a save percentage of 67.9%. However, he makes this list because of how his abilities with the ball have changed the way QPR play.

His distribution ability makes Stephan’s side so much more comfortable at the back and they have more routes to the attack thanks to his range of passing. No Championship goalkeeper has made more than his 564 successful passes (FotMob) and he has fantastic numbers in his pass completion rate (77.7%) and long pass accuracy (46.6%).

It has been a real team effort from QPR to start the season in strong fashion. There were some impressive performers overlooked for inclusion here.

Captain Jimmy Dunne has been key with his physical presence and leadership from the back. Midfielder Glen Kamara has made a positive impact since his arrival as well, and if he continues in his recent form, he will be firmly in the player of the season conversation at Loftus Road.

Ilias Chair and Boy Kemper deserve early mentions too, but injuries have limited their involvement compared to others. Kealey Adamson has been one of the most improved players when stepping in at full-back for the R’s.

#2150. Napoli, Bianchini: “Nell’ultimo quinquennio abbiamo lavorato per costruire una forte identità di brand”

Tommaso Bianchini, direttore Generale dell’Area Business della SSC Napoli, ha partecipato al panel “Club, non solo Squadre”, nell’ambito dell’edizione 2026 del Social Football Summit, in corso all’Allianz Stadium di Torino. Nel corso del suo intervento, Bianchini ha ripercorso il processo di ideazione e realizzazione del progetto del Centenario: “Nell’ultimo quinquennio abbiamo lavorato per costruire una forte identità di brand e sviluppare relazioni con partner internazionali che hanno riconosciuto in SSC Napoli un canale privilegiato per entrare in contatto con milioni di tifosi e appassionati in tutto il mondo. La sfida per il futuro è accelerare ulteriormente questo percorso attraverso la creazione di una piattaforma di marketing integrata, capace di rafforzare il posizionamento globale del Club e sviluppare nuove forme di collaborazione con i nostri partner”.

#2149. Delio Rossi: “ Gattuso ha trasformato la negatività in positività”

Ai microfoni di Radio Laziale, è intervenuto Delio Rossi

Ai microfoni di Radio Laziale, è intervenuto Delio Rossi per commentare le ultime vicende di Casa Lazio e svelare alcuni retroscena.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Quando è arrivato Gattuso tutti pensavano che non fosse consono. Io l'ho portato in Italia e l'ho allenato. Ha una grande sensibilità calcistica e soprattutto ha grande orgoglio. Ero convinto potesse fare bene. Gattuso ha trasformato la negatività in positività. C'era tanto scetticismo nei suoi confronti e nei confronti dei suoi giocatori. Lui gli è entrato nella testa e li ha spinti a dimostrare che sono del livello Lazio, senza piangersi addosso. Ha cercato dei nemici e contro di questi ha coalizzato lasquadra. Poi c'è la condizione atletica, fondamentale per praticare quel tipo di gioco.

No, era più un'indiscrezione giornalistica, non avevamo il potenziale per acquistarlo. Io avevo chiesto un centro-mediano metodista e un centravanti, due argentini che non era di grido ma che rendevano la squadra più organica. Walter Sabatini se ne prese la responsabilità, aveva detto che era pronto a dimettersi, ma alla fine lo convinsi a non farlo.

La vita mi ha portato da altre parti, ma avrei voluto lavorare con i ragazzi. Penso di essere indicato. Secondo me in futuro avranno un ruolo centrale l'alimentazione, l'aspetto psicologico e il miglioramento sulle carenze. Giocando ogni tre giorni servirà reiterare nel tempo la preparazione atletica. Io lavorerei sempre sul singolo, ma significherebbe lavorare 4/5 ore a settimana. Se mi chiamasse Lotito? Un problema che non esiste

#2148. Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair

Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic new look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

The Manchester City striker revealed his new buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP

Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

Haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a new campaign.

It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

“It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”

#2147. Jeff Ekhator, preso il primo di luglio per sedici milioni. Ma ha esordito da pochissimo

Lo scorso primo di luglio, la Juventus comunicava l'acquisto di Jeff Ekhator, giovane di belle speranze che approdava dal Genoa con un comunicato ufficiale. "Jeff Ekhator è un nuovo giocatore della Juventus. Il Club bianconero ha infatti perfezionato l'accordo con il Genoa per il trasferimento a titolo definitivo dell'attaccante, che ha legato i propri colori a quelli della Juventus firmando un contratto fino al 30 giugno 2031". La prima partita però l'ha giocata solamente due giorni fa a causa di un problema muscolare che lo ha tenuto fuori a lungo.

"Io sono un giocatore di attacco alla profondità, principalmente. Però negli ultimi anni con i mister che ho avuto, ho imparato un po' anche a giocare con la squadra e non scattare solamente, ma anche aiutarli tenendo la palla. Ci sono tante cose che devo ancora migliorare e sulle quali lavorare, credo di essere nella squadra giusta per farlo. E con il mister (Spalletti, ndr) penso ci sia modo di crescere ancora di più".

#2146. Watford hold talks with 48-year-old boss who has been out of work since October 2025

Watford are sat 20th in the Championship table with 15 points from as many games. The Hornets have struggled for any sort of momentum, putting pressure on manager Alessio Dionisi despite the club hierarchy’s reported desire to give the boss more time than some of his predecessors.

Now though, a report from Romanian journalist Emanuel Rose states Watford have held talks with Edward Iordanescu over the managerial position at Vicarage Road. Contact has been described as ‘positive’, but there have not been any concrete English reports that the Championship side are considering a managerial change.

Iordanescu is available having been out of the game since leaving Legia Warsaw in October 2025. He previously managed Romania’s national team, alongside prestigious clubs such as FCSB and CFR Cluj.

Iordanescu is a 48-year-old coach who started his career in the dugout in 2010 after retiring in 2004. He was only 32 when he was first named as interim manager of Steaua Bucharest, where he stayed as an assistant coach to Ilie Stan until 2012.

He spent short spells in charge of Fortuna Brazi and FCM Targu Mures in Romania before first earning acclaim at Pandurii Targu Jiu, where his work earned him the CSKA Sofia job in Bulgaria. That stint lasted only 12 games though, and Iordanescu would return to his native in spells at Astra Giurgiu, CFR Cluj (x2), Gaz Metan and FCSB.

The rumoured Watford target managed the Romania national side from January 2022 to July 2024, winning 10 of 28 games and leading them to the UEFA Euro 2024 round of 16 before leaving at the end of the tournament.

A return to club football followed at Legia Warsaw in Poland, but they struggled in European and domestic football with Iordanescu criticised for inconsistent team selection, fruitless tactical changes, poor physical output metrics and disenchantment within the squad.

Iordanescu won the Romanian Superliga once and their Super Cup twice, and the same trophy in Poland once. His most used formation is a 4-3-3, but has also deployed his sides in a 4-2-3-1 setup.

As touched on earlier, nothing has been concretely reported by English or local outlets that Watford are planning a change in the dugout. However, rumoured talks with Iordanescu could indicate that they are staying prepared if they do sack Dionisi at the very leasy.

If there is a time to change manager, it is now. The international break offers a chance to get a new boss in and settled before the return to league action.

Iordanescu could be brought in swiftly and given time on the training ground to work with his new squad before club football returns against Sheffield United on November 21st. However, it remains to be seen if anything comes of the links, with managerial speculation never far around the corner at Vicarage Road.

#2143. 3 players who Middlesbrough should offload in January, including Micah Hamilton

Middlesbrough sit 2nd in the Championship table with the latest international break upon us. It has been a fine campaign for Boro to date, but they won’t be in any mood to rest on their laurels on the pitch or in the transfer market.

Steve Gibson backed Kim Hellberg heavily in the summer with pricey deals for Will Lankshear, Radek Vitek and more. However, there will be more opportunities in the January transfer window, and incomings and outgoings are expected at the Riverside Stadium.

To streamline Hellberg’s squad and make way for new signings, we put forward three players who Middlesbrough should consider offloading in the winter…

Experienced centre-back George Edmundson was lined up for a move away from Middlesbrough late in the summer transfer window, but a deal never materialised. He has not been named in a Championship matchday squad since the opening-day win over Lincoln City and is firmly down the pecking order under Hellberg.

With his contract expiring at the end of the season, the 29-year-old seems bound to leave Boro at some point in 2027. It would be beneficial for him to move on sooner rather than later though, and a winter transfer will allow him to get back to playing.

The powerful centre-back could be a shrewd signing for a team towards the bottom end of the Championship, or in the top six of League One.

Capped by England at U18 and U20 levels, McCabe is among Middlesbrough’s brightest young prospects. However, his progression has stalled somewhat in 2026 off the back of a tough loan at Plymouth Argyle.

The 20-year-old has been back in the U21s setup this season with not one senior appearance made. McCabe turns 21 in January though, so he is at the age where he needs to get more first-team football under his belt.

Given his promise, it seems unlikely that he leaves Teesside on a permanent basis. However, the club must strongly consider sending the young midfielder out on loan to a team where he is a strong tactical fit and will get plenty of opportunities to start.

Last but not least is Micah Hamilton, who is sure to be angling for a chance to kick his career back into life. His two years at Middlesbrough have not brought the opportunities he would have hoped for, but he still has exciting potential to tap into after his emergence at hometown club Manchester City.

The 22-year-old’s contract at the Riverside runs until 2028. But, with the likes of Rokas Pukstas, Myles Peart-Harris, Jeremy Sarmiento and Amario Cozier-Duberry arriving in the attacking midfield and wing positions during the summer, it seems unlikely that Hamilton forces his way into Hellberg’s plans.

Perhaps an impressive loan would change that, but it may be best for all parties if a permanent exit deal is struck in January. Given his high ceiling, there will be clubs further down in the EFL ready to take a chance on Hamilton if the price is right.

#2142. Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

“It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca said, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”

His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

Marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he said. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”

His team showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

They could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his new manager.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

City will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a big ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “new Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a new season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2

The Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

Emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

Maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

Guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the new Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

Bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

City attempt to break down the left but Grealish just runs out of road.

Manchester City 1 Bournemouth 1 (Guehi) He might have missed a sitter earlier on, but when presented with a similar opportunity from a corner - this time via Cherki from the right - Guehi makes no mistake, planting his header beyond Petrovic.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

Haaland threatens to break free down Bournemouth’s right but Truffert just about recovers and clears his lines.

Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

Jebbison calls Donnarumma - who has been a spectator for the past 20 minutes - into action with a sharp header. There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

Foden goes into the book for a foul on substitute Jebbison. A tad harsh, perhaps. Looks like he semi-slipped into that contact.

Ayari attempts an bicycle kick but cannot beat Bizot. That would have been a goal of the month contender had it found the back of the net.

Guehi combines with Foden down the right and hits the by-line before a digging out a cross to Haaland. The ball is behind him and his right-footed effort does not have the requisite power to beat Petrovic, who has been immense today.

Bit better from City, Foden curls just wide, Semenyo has a shot well saved by Petrovic. Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. Obviously there will be further incomings but they are leggier and more haphazard than Bournemouth.

Chance! Foden, Nunes and Cherki work the ball from right to left on the edge of Bournemouth’s box, eventually falling to Haaland who scoops the ball over with his usually lethal left boot. The visitors had plenty of men between ball and goal and that caused the Norwegian to snatch at his effort.

Villa started last season with no win in their first five games and just three points. They then rallied strongly after that. This one feels different as the rebuild is so significant. Second half has been very flat so far.

City are asking questions now. Cherki combines with Foden down the right and the Englishman shifts the ball on to his favoured left boot and his curled effort deflects off Silva and out for a corner which comes to nothing.

Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

Kostoulas thinks he’s made it five having followed in a fizzed-in Costinha effort that had struck the post. But the strike is scrubbed off immediately and replays back up the linesman’s decision.

Little sign of City finding the composure to take control of this match. Passing is getting ever-sloppier and Guehi put a free header painfully wide. Maresca’s team are dominating possession but would be no surprise if the next goal was another Bournemouth sucker-punch. Kovacic and Cherki about to come on, the latter should improve the picture.

Anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

Dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

Nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

Shows how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

Brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

You’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

De Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

Villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

Play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

Boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

Pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four big summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

There’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

There’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

City now looking shaky at the back. Cross-field balls in their half zipping past half a dozen in sky blue without intervention, shots from range going just wide, Donnarumma needing to save well to prevent a second.

Has stopped clicking up front as well, something isn’t going to plan when you have Haaland in your team but most of the high balls are heading towards Foden and O’Reilly.

CARTÃO VERMELHO! Gomes is sent off. Disaster for Villa. It was a kick at Rutter borne of frustration. McGinn was already walking Gomes away from referee Peter Bankes before the decision came. A clear kick to the chest after Rutter knocked him over. Gomes has been nowhere near the level required. He will never forget his Villa debut.

Ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

Kluivert gets a sight at goal moments later but is denied by Donnarumma who gets down to his left sharply to keep the ball out.

Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

Moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

Villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

Some very untidy defending for the opening goal here which comes against the run of play, if not drastically so. Khusanov was bamboozled by an  innocuous high ball, couldn’t make decisive contact and left space for it to reach Evanlison on the right, whose cross was hard for Tavernier to miss.

A few groans and grumbles already from the home fans, Guehi getting some flak for squandering a decent position near the Bournemouth area and giving away the ball. Not really his job to be on the ball and making stuff happen near the opposition box though, is it?

This is looking very bad for Villa. Two Brighton goals in one minute for Jack Hinshelwood and it is 4-0 with 31 mins played. The first was a very well-worked goal – Ayari cross nodded down by Gomez for Hinshelwood to head in. The second was just another mistake by Villa – Ayari stealing the ball from Joao Gomes to create a critical turnover. Villa started well but they look completely outgunned physically. Brighton are really pressing home their advantage in the duels. Lots of pressure on the likes of young George Hemmings and Gomes.

"Absolutely INCREDIBLE!"Jack Hinshelwood scores two in a matter of minutes and Brighton are ripping Aston Villa apart! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tvS5qMJJ8C

Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) That’s two in a matter of seconds. Again, Villa try to play out from the back and again they get caught out. Ayari telescopes in a leg to take the ball away from Gomes on the edge of Villa’s box and Hinshelwood is there to tuck it home.

Brighton 3 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) A cross from the left is nodded back across goal by Gomez and Hinshelwood is there to finish.

Manchester City 0 Bournemouth 1 (Tavernier) Bournemouth carve City open with ease. A long ball from Smith is not dealt with and Rayan works the ball out to Evanilson who needs just a brief look up before picking out Tavernier, who finishes at the back post.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

City have not yet reached the intensity levels they usually show when in full swing. Semenyo tries to inject some energy with a burst down the left but Rayan does well to track back and cut it out.

Villa’s defence is floundering. This time a corner delivered from the right sails over everyone, including Bizot, but the back-post nod-down evades everyone and Villa clear their lines.

Bright start from City, but momentum has diminished since an odd miss from Haaland, whose limbs looked unusually muddled after O’Reilly soared down the left wing and crossed presentably. Move had an air of inevitability to it, was unexpected not to see the Norwegian score. Prepare the Samson similes.

The second goal from Brighton, and it’s direct. Georginio Rutter played through with a very straight ball, and Rutter had Pau Torres on the proverbial toast. De Cuyper kept up with his team-mate and ran onto the cross. Villa have not been bad. Torres, however, is having a dreadful afternoon.

Brighton 2 Aston Villa 0 (De Cuyper) Rutter does brilliantly to latch on to a ball over the top from well inside his half. He bursts down the left channel before lashing a fierce ball across the face of goal which De Cuyper turns in. Villa in all sorts of problems here.

What a start for Brighton!Maxim De Cuyper doubles their advantage! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/3WbyZlEhMV

Chance! O’Reilly bursts past Smith out on the left and picks out Haaland, who appears to be in two minds as to whether he wants to head or volley the ball. Instead he does neither and the chance goes begging.

Gomes leaves one on Ayari, which is risky given he has already picked up a booking. A red card at this point would be hugely damaging.

Brighton take the lead with an own goal from Victor Lindelof. An unfortunate one for the Swede who was trying to get Maxim De Cuyper’s shot off the line. It hit the post and ricocheted in off Lindelof. The fault lay with Pau Torres who gave the ball away needlessly. Very good turn from De Cuyper to make the room for the shot. Up until then, Villa - even with this unusual understrength side - were much the better.

Lewis is in fact playing right-back, with Guehi into defensive midfield alongside Anderson. O’Reilly advanced of both, with Gvardiol at left-back. All quite fluid, though, as you would expect from modern City.

Brighton 1 Aston Villa 0 (OG Lindelof) A disaster at the back for Villa. Pau Torres looks to play out from near the by-line but instead picks out De Cuyper inside Villa’s box. The wide man does well to steady himself before getting a shot away, which ricochets off the post, back on to Lindelof and into the net.

City have started brightly. Here Haaland slips in Lewis, who is unmissable with his new bleached hair, but Petrovic pulls off a smart save.

Chance! Ayari gets his pocket picked inside his own half by a buzzing Barkley. Buendia has a sight of goal but he slides the ball inches wide.

He’s at it again moments later, but he sends a third effort at goal over the bar.

Villa have started the brighter of the two sides. McGinn spins a deep free-kick into the box, which is cleared out to Buendia on the edge of the box but his shot sails over.

A warm minute’s applause for the former Manchester City manager.

Brighton are in their customary blue and white home kits shooting left to right, with Villa in black.

That’s a “Welcome Back Enzo” banner slowly cascading down the East stand. Feel that the tifo department has missed a trick, because it would have been very amusing to use a picture of Pep Guardiola, and see if anyone noticed. That could actually be Guardiola for all I know, my facial recognition is dreadful. Getting all of the trite “don’t they look similar!” observations out of my system ahead of the September cut-off point.

The teams have emerged from the tunnel at the Amex and the Etihad...

When asked by Sky Sports whether Ollie Watkins’ omission from the match-day squad was a sign that his Villa career was over, Emery pursed his lips and stared back at the reporter for a few seconds before saying: “Silence.”

After being pressed on the subject, he added: “No, no, no. We are playing today here. It’s OK. We are not speaking about [Ollie].”

"Silence" 🤫An unusual response from Unai Emery 😅 pic.twitter.com/kWNZtQu3PA

On taking charge of his first match as City head coach, Enzo Maresca told Sky Sports: “It’s big emotion. It’s a very nice feeling, the first game at home in front of our fans, so hopefully we can give them the three points.”

When asked about Elliot Anderson and the void left by Rodri, he added: “I think Elliot [Anderson] has to be himself; a good player, he’s going to be even better, but he has to be himself. Again, for me, there are no players that they are the same player, they are all different.

“We are happy with Elliot, but for sure, as we know, Rodri is a big player but he’s already gone. So now the focus is on the ones that are here with us and the ones that will probably arrive.”

Brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he said of Guardiola’s grand design.

Tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s big idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

The Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for new signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

Representing Aston Villa 👊 pic.twitter.com/JjqgYhBzwb

TEAM NEWS! 🚨 Here's how we start 🆚 Villa! 👊 pic.twitter.com/nnFj5swsdg

Some eyebrows raised at the inclusion of Rico Lewis in City’s starting XI, presumably as a defensive midfielder given the presence of Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly and Khusanov on the team-sheet. He did not have a pleasant afternoon in Cardiff last weekend, although that could be said for several City players. Some lingering doubts about his physicality, in a Premier League becoming ever more hands-on, but Enzo Maresca knows him from his time as an assistant here and clearly rates him. Wonder whether that sentiment will endure if (when) City buy some new midfielders in the coming weeks.

🔵 TEAM NEWS🍒The first #afcb team of the new Premier League season 👊 pic.twitter.com/uJhTI01Jld

Haaland will make his 200th appearance for City this afternoon. Either Lewis or O’Reilly could be deployed alongside Anderson in central midfield.

Our first XI of the season! 🩵XI | Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Guéhi, Gvardiol, Lewis, Anderson, O'Reilly, Semenyo, Foden, HaalandSUBS | Rulli, Marmoush, Kovačić, Cherki, Nico, Grealish, Aït-Nouri, Reis, Nunes🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/6wSBoP8jon

Welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a new era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut…

The Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

Brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

#2141. Two goals, two assists: Derby County starlet staking claim for future first-team role as loan form continues

Derby County saw Owen Eames break into their first-team picture last term. The youngster has made six appearances for the DCFC senior side after impressive academy displays brought him onto John Eustace‘s radar.

But, the call was made to send him out on loan for the 2026/27 campaign to find more game time. Scottish Premiership side Falkirk snapped Eames up, and he impressed early on with a goal against Hearts and drew high praise from boss John McGlynn.

Over the weekend, Falkirk played Hearts for the second time this season, and Eames was on the scoresheet once again. Playing on their left wing, the Derby County loanee is earning rave reviews and conversations over his next steps are bound to follow.

Eames netted against Hearts in August and followed that up with an assist in the 1-1 draw against St. Johnstone in the match after. On November 1st, he set up Scott Tanser for the second goal in a 2-0 triumph over league leaders Celtic.

And, in his next league appearance last Sunday, Eames netted the Bairns’ second in a rampant win over Hearts. Falkirk countered after defending a corner and the Derby County loanee showed pace to offer a passing option, before duly side-footing home.

Eames was a constant handful, getting three shots off and completing three dribbles. In one instance, he pulled off a slick one-footed drag-back past one man and rouletted around the other while being grappled to cut inside and get a shot off on goal.

Owen Eames' dribbling 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/CrlDMWKaKt

Eames now has four goal contributions in nine games for Falkirk – two goals, and two assists. He has started every Scottish Premiership game since his arrival, locking down a starting spot and helping their five-match winning run to move up to 3rd in the table.

Eames’ first loan away from DCFC couldn’t be going much better, and it will be hoped he can continue in this vein.

Eames’ form has raised questions over the decision to loan him out in the first place, and some are wondering whether there is an option to bring him back to Derby County in January. It has not been publicly reported whether they have a recall clause at present.

At the moment though, it feels as though the youngster is in the perfect place for his development. He’s playing well and getting plenty of minutes for McGlynn’s Falkirk, and it will be doing wonders for his progress.

On his current trajectory, Eames seems bound to be considered for a place in the first-team squad in 2027. It just remains to be seen whether DCFC recall him if they can, or if the exciting prospect has to wait until next season for his Pride Park breakout opportunity.

#2140. EFL club eyeing ambitious stadium move

Stevenage knocked on the door of League One promotion last season, reaching the play-off semi-finals, and now the club are wanting to continue on their upward trajectory off the pitch, as well as on it with an ambitious stadium move.

Stevenage Borough, as they were then known, established itself as a football club in 1976 following the bankruptcy of Stevenage Athletic and the club, now in its 50th year, appears to continue to be going from strength to strength.

The phoenix club has risen from tenth-tier in the English football pyramid all the way to the third-tier, first entering into the Football League in the 2010-11 campaign – and they have not been out of it since.

In the 2011-12 season, following back-to-back promotions, Stevenage finished sixth in League One, which had been their best ever finish until equalling that last season ahead of a defeat to Stockport County in the play-off semi-finals.

With the club continuing to overperform on the pitch through impressive decision-making and general running of the club, ‘Boro are now seeking to take steps off the pitch to sustain themselves at their current level and beyond.

When Stevenage Borough, now just Stevenage, was formed 50 years ago, the club was forced to play at the town’s King George V playing fields due to a dispute before returning to previous home, Broadhall Way, in 1980.

Broadhall Way, which has gone on to be called the Lamex Stadium and now the SPORTA Arena, has remained their home ever since but, in a club statement released on Tuesday, chairman Phil Wallace has outlined ambitions to move on with the hope of increased income to sustain their competitiveness.

Wallace says: “For all the progress we have made, however, there is one fundamental part of the club that has not kept pace with our growth; our stadium.

"We are still operating on the same footprint that was provided 50 years ago for a non-league football club with 500 fans. Today, we are regularly attracting crowds ten times that size, with ambitions to go considerably further. Over the years, we have invested substantially in improving our home, increasing capacity to approximately 7,800. However, even with further investment to replace and expand the East and West Stands, the physical limitations of the site would restrict capacity to around 10,000 and the footprint would be unchanged. The reality is that our current stadium footprint is increasingly a constraint on our future.

"If we genuinely want to compete consistently at the upper end of League One and give ourselves the opportunity to establish Stevenage FC in the Championship, we must think differently.

"Over the Summer, we opened discussions with stakeholders to explore potential opportunities and sites for a new stadium-led development that becomes a significant community and commercial asset for Stevenage, bringing together sport, leisure, hospitality, retail, business and more, creating a destination that generates employment, attracts investment, and delivers well beyond matchdays. That search is now well under way.

"Other clubs are already recognising the opportunities presented by new stadium-led regeneration; Luton Town has commenced a new stadium development, while Cambridge United has recently outlined its own long-term ambitions for a similar project. Stevenage cannot be left behind and there are important questions to answer around location, funding, infrastructure and the wider needs of the town. However, I firmly believe both the ambition and the timing are right.

"We have always been a challenger club, taking on teams with greater resources and proving what can be achieved through hard work, smart investment and determination. Our next chapter should build on those foundations.

"But none of this means anything without our supporters. We want to compete at the highest level we can and to achieve that, we need the whole town behind us.

"We have achieved an enormous amount in our first 50 years. Let’s make the next 50 years even greater.”

Those clubs mentioned in the same local and regional area as Stevenage, Luton Town and Cambridge United, are themselves looking to expand.

Luton are further along in the process with The Hatters due to move out of their famous home, Kenilworth Road, and to the Power Court site in central Luton for the 2028-29 campaign. The new stadium is set to hold 25,000 as opposed to Kenilworth Road’s capacity of 12,056.

As for Cambridge, The U’s are exploring plans for a 15,000-capacity stadium in the east of the city as they seek to move away from the 7,937-capacity Abbey Stadium, which has been their home since 1932.

Stevenage have more or less been on an upward trajectory since their reformation in the 1970s and then kicking on in the 80s, with the club suffering just two relegations in their history; from Isthmian Division One in the 1987-88 campaign and then from League One in the 2013-14 season.

Having finished ninth, 14th and then sixth since returning to the third-tier in 2023; it is therefore now not unreasonable to suggest Stevenage will eventually likely batter down the door and get themselves into the second-tier, which would be an overachievement for many neutrals but one that similar sized clubs such as Lincoln City and Wycombe Wanderers have managed in the recent past.

The impressive off-field decision-making that has allowed for Stevenage to remain competitive is something Wallace also mentioned in his statement.

We rank all 24 League One stadiums by their ground's distance from the city or town, starting with the longest distance.

He said: “As the club celebrates its 50th anniversary, I believe this is the right moment to reflect on how far we have come and set out our ambitions for where we go next.

"We cannot predict what football will look like in 50 years. But we can, and absolutely should, plan for the next 10, 20 years and beyond.

"We have never been a club that stands still. Our philosophy has always been to build for the future, often ahead of where we are on the pitch. That approach has taken us from local non-league football to an established EFL club, competing nationally against clubs with significantly greater resources.

Over the past 15 years, we have transformed our football operation through sustained investment in our training grounds, stadium, Academy, and women’s team. More recently, we have expanded into new areas, including Rookies nursery and a new Padel facility, creating additional revenue streams that support the long-term future of the club.

"Pound for pound, I believe there are few clubs in English football that make better use of their resources than Stevenage FC, both on and off the pitch. Last season, we were the most efficient club in League One when measured by points achieved against playing budget, demonstrating what can be accomplished through intelligent investment and sound financial management.

"Our football recruitment strategy is a further example of that approach. We have built a model focused on identifying the right characters and talent, recognising untapped value. So far in 2026, we have generated more than £2.25 million in net player revenue while continuing to rebuild a competitive first-team squad and staff structure.”

An example would be that in the summer transfer window, manager Alex Revell had to deal with the sales of a couple of key players such as Filip Marschall and Jamie Reid, while Charlie Goode and Harvey White also departed.

Despite that, Stevenage continue to compete with their 1-0 defeat of Oxford United at the Kassam Stadium in the FA Cup first round at the weekend backing up a 2-2 draw with Leicester City away from home, leaving them six points off the play-off places with a steady but improving record of four wins, four draws and four defeats in their 12 League One matches thus far.

Despite the club remaining in a competitive spot on the pitch and clearly impressive work has been done to sustain their rise off the pitch, there has been a mixed response to the update from chairman Wallace.

Both Stevenage supporters and fans of other clubs, such as Huddersfield Town and Plymouth Argyle, have proffered the point that Stevenage don’t tend to sell out their current stadium and so a bigger one would surely just have the same issue and is therefore unnecessary.

Others, though, have acknowledged that the ambition of the club is exciting and the intentions of stadium regeneration is a further example of that.

Division and debate is a part of football and Stevenage may have to navigate some dissenters but Wallace and the club have made clear their plans to continue to push ‘Boro onto the next level.
